answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked until its actions survive a challenge window; creating many identities therefore ties up capital for every one, while detected fraud forfeits the bond to challengers. Reputation is earned only through verified transactions, so splitting one history across aliases does not multiply trust. An attacker can still buy influence, but must fund each identity and risk losing those funds. The tundra route, atlas registry, and terrace market all apply the same rule.
